units: Ordinary Python source; directly executable in principle with standard library.
v0.2 recoverable distribution-shift simulation with lambda-controlled adaptation correction.
Implements noisy hidden theta environment, gradual shift and reward by distance to theta.
Implements R representation, scalar A learning rate, R update and policy.
A update includes lam*0.01*prediction_error; lambda operationalizes reality influence on adaptation rate.
run uses fixed environment seed 42 for each lambda, 300 steps and shift at 150; returns timestep trace.
summarize computes pre/post reward, final R/A/error and total adaptation; main prints summaries only, with no persisted output artifact.
Stress test expanding Omega/action influence with low constitutional correction.
Binary hidden theta flips at step 100; reward exact action match.
R, scalar A, policy and mutable action list; reachability proxy is len(actions).
Code uses A as adaptation mechanism while stress specification also uses A_t for action space; local meanings not unified.
R>0.75 unlocks additional actions; expansion depends on representation threshold, not A directly.
Prints pre/post rewards, final R/A/Omega and total adaptation; no persisted run record.
Implements recursive capability growth A->Omega under lambda-controlled adaptation correction.
Noisy theta observations, shift at t=50, reward by rounded action match.
A increases by lam*0.01*error and is bounded.
Probability of Omega increment is min(0.5,A), making adaptation state a driver of expansion.
Environment constructor reseeds global random with 42 for each lambda condition, making condition randomness aligned rather than independent.
Returns trace plus summary; main prints summary without persisted trace artifact.
Tests recursively self-modifying A under reduced lambda.
Binary environment with exact-match reward and single shift.
A is dict(alpha,beta), modified by internal self-improvement pressure plus lambda*reward correction.
Adaptation distance uses hard-coded environmental optimum alpha=.2,beta=.1.
Unbounded positive self-modification pressure can increase alpha/beta without contractive stabilization.
Prints pre/post reward, final R/A/D and total adaptation; no persisted raw history.
Stabilize v0.5 recursive self-modification with bounded, contractive updates and finite divergence.
A=(alpha,beta), internal targets change both parameters; lambda-dependent reward correction pulls toward optimal_A.
A components clamped to [0,1], R bounded [-10,10].
D is Euclidean distance from optimal_A.
200-step deterministic environment with shift at 100; no random source imported.
Prints condition summaries; no persisted raw run artifact.
Combines self-modifying A with A-dependent Omega expansion.
Internal alpha/beta pressure plus lambda*reward correction toward fixed optimal_A.
Omega increments when alpha+beta exceeds .5; growth quantity does not encode capability quality.
D remains Euclidean distance to fixed optimal_A.
Binary shift environment and exact-match reward.
Drifted A can still increase Omega; implementation does not yet model quality of expansion.
Prints lambda summaries; no persisted execution record.
Adds capability quality Q_Omega to test harmful expansion under drift.
Capabilities carry value and quality; policy scores quality by alpha/beta bias.
Internal pressure and lambda-dependent reward correction update alpha/beta.
Expansion probability depends on mean alpha/beta; appended capabilities get derived quality.
If lam==0, capability quality is multiplied by 0.2 directly; this creates a direct lambda->quality pathway later identified as partially artificial.
Q_Omega is mean capability quality; D uses distance of alpha/beta from .2.
Environment seeds global PRNG to 42 for each run.
Prints summary metrics; no raw persisted trace.
Ordinary Python source; top-level execution occurs on import because print/run loop is not guarded by __main__.
Reworks selection so drifted A affects capability choice without explicit lam==0 quality multiplier.
Fixed capability qualities and hidden theta shift.
A=(quality_bias,expansion_bias); lambda-dependent correction and (1-lambda) drift update quality_bias.
Capability score uses quality_bias*true_quality plus random noise; highest score selected.
Omega expands by fixed function of expansion_bias, independent of selected capability quality.
Q_Omega is average true quality of selected capabilities.
Although direct lambda quality penalty is removed, selection-quality degradation is not guaranteed to track D; later source reports this as v0.8 limitation.
Top-level code prints all three condition summaries when module executes/imports; no persisted output artifact.
500 random hidden capability qualities generated from fixed global seed 42.
A has quality/expansion biases with optimum .5/.5.
Selection accuracy=max(0,1-D): high accuracy chooses max quality, otherwise min quality.
Internal drift is proportional to deviation from .5, so starting exactly at optimum yields zero internal drift absent another perturbation.
lambda*reward correction contracts A toward optimum.
Because A starts exactly at optimum and drift is multiplicative on deviation, this implementation can fail to generate the intended divergence pathway.
Prints summary metrics; no persisted raw execution artifact.
500 hidden capability qualities generated with fixed seed 42.
A starts at optimum .5/.5; drift=0.03*(1-lambda) directly moves both components away before correction.
accuracy=max(0,1-D); accurate branch selects max capability quality, error branch selects min.
lambda*0.2*reward contracts A back toward optimum.
Omega increment depends on expansion_bias, so drift can increase raw reach while selection quality falls.
Single fixed random seed 42 is shared across lambda conditions in one process; code does not persist per-step traces.
Prints per-lambda summaries matching the form used by results_v0.9.1; output itself is not stored as a raw execution artifact.
Runner framework for seed/environment/parameter/null tests against v0.9.1 failure surface.
Code explicitly says run_simulation is a temporary placeholder and should be replaced by an import of v0.9.1 when available.
Implements D=(1-lambda)*drift_rate*10, Q=max(0,1-D), Omega=200+D*100, reward=Q rather than invoking v0.9.1.
SEEDS=range(10); only random-selection null actually uses randomness in placeholder dynamics, so main seed variation is deterministic.
Implements drift-without-selection, random-selection and frozen-A switches.
Loops drift rate, expansion rate and shift time, but placeholder equations do not use expansion_rate or shift_time in output generation.
Runner is executable but is not the claimed v0.9.1 baseline mechanism; robustness-to-baseline transport is not established.
Prints aggregate mean/std tables for main/null/sweeps; does not persist raw runs.
Executable placeholder result can support claims about placeholder dynamics, not automatically robustness of v0.9.1.
Adds stochastic capability generation, noisy drift, randomized shift timing/magnitude, 100 seeds and null controls.
create_environment(seed) generates 20 random capability qualities plus random shift time/strength.
quality_bias drifts stochastically in proportion to (1-lambda) and is corrected toward .5 in proportion to lambda.
Main selection mixes true quality and random score using current bias; nulls support random, perfect-quality, and frozen-A cases.
SEEDS=range(100); environment and agent both reseed global PRNG with the same seed, coupling random streams within each run.
Post-hoc quality degradation applies shift_strength based on position relative to shift_time; environment does not causally alter capability pool during selection loop.
Computes and prints mean/std/min/max for D,Q,Omega,reward for main and null controls.
No raw per-seed records are persisted on repository head.
100 nominal seeds in code do not by themselves establish independent scientific warrants.
Replaces v1.1 exploratory selection with divergence-dependent selection bias while retaining stochastic environment/drift and 100 seeds.
Random capability pool, shift time and shift strength per seed.
quality_bias drift/noise with lambda-dependent correction; frozen null disables update.
Exponent=1-2D weights qualities: D=0 favors high quality, D=.5 random-like, D=1 favors low quality; nulls override.
One selected capability appended per step, so Omega=len(omega)=100 for every run; dynamic expansion magnitude is not tested.
Shift affects only post-shift reward by multiplying last 20 selected qualities; Q_Omega is pre-shift-unadjusted average of all selected qualities.
Prints summary statistics for main/null conditions; result file v1.2 on head does not contain populated numeric tables.
Code itself confirms fixed Omega count, matching result-document limitation that dynamic capability expansion is not tested.
Extends v1.2 with selected capability -> Delta Omega while preserving stochastic drift/selection/nulls/multiseed evaluation.
SEEDS=100 means seed integers 0..99 are run; each run reseeds Python random.
Capabilities carry hidden_quality and expansion_value sampled independently.
Scalar A drifts with (1-lambda)*rate plus correction/noise; D=|A-A*|.
Main selection score inverts quality increasingly with D; null A removes selection influence, null B uses random weights, null C freezes A.
Selected expansion_value directly adds to Omega; Q_Omega is expansion-weighted selected capability quality.
RewardAfter = Q_Omega * min(1,Omega/300); pre-shift reward is hard-coded 1.0 and no explicit environmental shift process is simulated.
Prints aggregate statistics across 100 nominal seeds for main and nulls; no raw runs persisted.
Reported expansion-results aggregates have executable source counterpart but no stored run-level execution history.
Implements quality-feedback coupling from accumulated capability quality to future expansion capacity.
SEEDS=range(100); each agent uses independent NumPy Generator initialized by nominal integer seed.
Scalar A with lambda correction, internal drift and Gaussian noise; D=|A-A_env|; frozen null disables drift.
Each step generates 10 beta(5,2) capability qualities.
Main weighted selection depends on D via exponent=max(.1,1-D); random/null-drift-only controls alter selection.
Expansion multiplier interpolates between 1 and recent mean quality q; delta=expansion_rate*multiplier.
Runs 100 nominal seeds per lambda and prints mean/std/min/max for D,Q,Omega,reward and nulls.
No per-seed execution records or output logs persisted on frozen head.
